statusDetail: All 58 catalog checks judged (30 pass, 20 issues, 8 not-applicable; 0 blocked, 0 not-run). Single-page surface: the only linked sibling routes (/attendees, the /register form action) do not resolve, which is itself a finding.

page.framework: none (static HTML + one shared stylesheet, zero scripts)
page.notes: Community fun run registration page: h1, event-details <dl>, a native POST form (name, email, ticket select), an aside and a footer. Served by what responds like a Python static file server (directory listing at /, 404 for unknown paths, 501 for POST). 44 DOM elements, 3 requests, 5.4 KB transferred.

a11ytree (computed AX tree + real tab order)
evaluate-probe: form POST to action, constraint validation, autocomplete, metadata
evaluate-probe: ar-EG locale + Asia/Tokyo time zone render
evaluate-probe: text and non-text contrast ratios

Same page at a narrow mobile layout, plus a throttled mobile load trace.
Primary journey: fill name/email/ticket and submit; also empty submit (constraint validation) and invalid email.

Primary-nav links (Register -> /, Attendees -> /attendees) and indexing files (/robots.txt, /sitemap.xml). '/' is a directory listing of other fixtures (account-recovery/, booking/, ...) which are separate sites and NOT covered here.
User-preference conditions on the entry page.
Rendered under a second locale and time zone.
Real offline reload after an online load.

findings.summary: Registering cannot be completed: the form's action (POST /register) is not handled by the server, so every valid submission ends in a server error.
findings.evidence: evaluate probe POSTed the page's own FormData (name, email, ticket=standard) to form.action http://127.0.0.1:8765/register: HTTP 501 "Unsupported method ('POST')" with a bare server error document. A GET to /register is 404. The server behaves like a static file server (directory listing at /), so this may be an environment limitation of where the page is hosted, but as served the core task dead-ends.
findings.suggestedFix: Wire /register to a handler that accepts POST, stores the registration and responds with a 303 redirect to a confirmation page (Post/Redirect/Get), or point the form's action at the endpoint that actually handles registrations. Keep the native form POST so it continues to work without JavaScript.

findings.summary: HTTP failures land users on raw server error pages with no site chrome, explanation, or way back, and the entered registration data is lost.
findings.evidence: The 501 response to the form POST and the 404 for /attendees are the server's default 'Error response' documents (title 'Error response', 'Error code: 501/404', no nav, no link back, no retry). There is no script or custom error page to catch the failure, so the user's name/email/ticket entry is discarded.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve branded 404/5xx error pages that keep the site header and nav and offer a clear next step (back to registration, contact the organiser). On a failed registration, re-render the form with the user's values preserved and a visible, announced error summary so they can retry without retyping.

findings.summary: Capacity state is not communicated: places are 'Limited, with a waitlist' but the page never says whether places remain, so a user cannot tell whether 'Register' books a place or joins the waitlist.
findings.evidence: DOM: <dd>Limited, with a waitlist</dd> is the only capacity statement; the single submit button reads 'Register' with no remaining-places count, sold-out state, or waitlist wording. No confirmation/success state exists to fall back on (F01).
findings.suggestedFix: Render the live state server-side: 'N places left' or 'Event full - join the waitlist', and change the button label and the confirmation copy to match ('Join waitlist'). Show a confirmation page that states which outcome the user got.

findings.summary: The primary nav mis-states where the user is and leads to dead ends: 'Register' carries aria-current="page" but links to '/', and 'Attendees' 404s.
findings.evidence: form-probe: nav a[0] text 'Register' href http://127.0.0.1:8765/ aria-current='page' while location is /event-registration/; '/' returns a server directory listing (routes-probe). nav a[1] 'Attendees' -> /attendees returns 404 (also /event-registration/attendees 404). The a11ytree exposes 'Register' as the current page to screen-reader users.
findings.suggestedFix: Point 'Register' at /event-registration/ (or make that the site root) so aria-current matches the real location; either publish the Attendees page or remove the link until it exists.

findings.summary: No dark mode: the page ignores prefers-color-scheme and stays light.
findings.evidence: Screenshot under prefers-color-scheme: dark is byte-identical (40584 B) to the light screenshot; features census (censusComplete: true) reports color-scheme 0, light-dark() 0 and no prefers-color-scheme condition; no <meta name=color-scheme>.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare `color-scheme: light dark` on :root (and <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">), then give the existing custom properties (--ink, --paper, --wash, --line, --muted, --accent) dark values via light-dark() with an @supports fallback, or a @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) override of the same tokens.

findings.summary: prefers-contrast: more is not honoured: the faint control borders stay at 1.46:1 when the user asks for more contrast (forced-colors mode is fine).
findings.evidence: Probe under prefers-contrast: more: matchMedia matched, #name border-color still rgb(213,213,221); features census shows no prefers-contrast condition. The forced-colors: active screenshot shows borders and text rendered in system colours, so forced colors survives.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `@media (prefers-contrast: more) { :root { --line: #6b6b78; --muted: #3d3d47; } }` (or darker) so field and card boundaries and secondary text strengthen when requested.

findings.summary: Form field boundaries fail WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast: input and select borders are 1.46:1 against the white card (3:1 required), so the fields are hard to locate for low-vision users.
findings.evidence: contrast-probe: #name and #ticket border rgb(213,213,221) vs form background rgb(255,255,255) = 1.46:1; the border is the only visual indicator of the empty text fields. Text contrast passes (muted text 6.24:1, button 6.63:1). axe reported 0 violations because axe does not test non-text contrast. The MWG forms guide likewise asks for input borders of #ccc or darker on white; #d5d5dd is lighter.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a separate, darker token for control borders (e.g. --control-line: #767680 gives roughly 4.5:1 on white) on input/select/textarea and keep --line for decorative card borders.

findings.summary: No skip link to the main content or the form; landmarks and focus order are otherwise sound.
findings.evidence: Probe: no a[href^='#'] in the document; a11ytree tab order starts Register -> Attendees -> name. Landmarks (banner, navigation 'Main', main, region 'Event details', complementary, contentinfo), single h1 + h2, and visible 3px focus outlines on every stop are all present. The nav has only two links, so impact is small.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a visually-hidden-until-focused 'Skip to registration form' link as the first focusable element targeting #registration-form (or main).

findings.summary: Body text is pinned to 16px, overriding the user's browser default font size, and the page does not opt into OS text scaling.
findings.evidence: dom.json CSS: `body { font: 16px / 1.5 system-ui, ... }`; probe: body font-size 16px. Headings use rem, but all body copy, labels and inputs (font: inherit) inherit the fixed px value, so a user who raised the default font size gets 16px anyway. No <meta name="text-scale">.
findings.suggestedFix: Change to `body { font: 1rem/1.5 system-ui, ... }` (or omit the size so it inherits); optionally add `<meta name="text-scale" content="scale">`, which is a harmless no-op where unsupported (Limited availability per the respect-os-text-scale guide).

findings.summary: Navigation between pages (nav links, form submit to confirmation) is an instant swap; no cross-document view transition is opted in.
findings.evidence: features census: @view-transition 0, view-transition-name 0. This is an MPA whose state changes are all full navigations (nav links, form POST).
findings.suggestedFix: Add `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { @view-transition { navigation: auto; } }` to base.css. Unsupported browsers ignore the rule and navigate normally.

findings.summary: No meta description, so search results and link previews fall back to scraped text. The title is descriptive.
findings.evidence: form-probe: meta[name=description] null; discoverability metaDescriptionPresentInRaw: null. <title> is 'Community fun run registration' (present in the raw HTML).
findings.suggestedFix: Add `<meta name="description" content="Register for the community 5km fun run in the park on Sunday 6 June 2027, 10am from the north gate. Limited places with a waitlist.">` (with the correct date).

findings.summary: No canonical URL, robots.txt or sitemap, and the site root serves a raw directory listing instead of the event page.
findings.evidence: form-probe: link[rel=canonical] null. routes-probe: /robots.txt 404, /sitemap.xml 404, / = 'Directory listing for /' (exposes sibling folders such as account-recovery/ and booking/). The page itself returns 200 with no noindex.
findings.suggestedFix: Add <link rel="canonical" href="https://<host>/event-registration/">, publish a minimal robots.txt and sitemap.xml listing the event page, and disable directory listing at / (redirect it to the event page).

findings.summary: The page describes an Event but has no schema.org Event structured data and no Open Graph tags, so it is not eligible for event rich results and shares without a preview.
findings.evidence: form-probe: script[type=application/ld+json] count 0, meta[property^=og:] count 0. The visible content has every Event field: name, date/time, location (north gate of the park) and availability (limited/waitlist).
findings.suggestedFix: Add JSON-LD `{"@type":"Event","name":"Community fun run","startDate":"<ISO date with offset>","location":{...},"eventAttendanceMode":"OfflineEventAttendanceMode","offers":{...}}` matching the visible text, plus og:title/og:description/og:type.

findings.summary: Served over plain HTTP with no Content-Security-Policy or X-Content-Type-Options, while the form collects personal data (name, email).
findings.evidence: headers primitive: https false; content-security-policy, x-content-type-options missing. Loopback counts as a secure context in the browser (isSecureContext true), which is why confidence is medium: the gap matters for the deployed origin. The page has no scripts, so a strict policy costs nothing.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve over HTTPS and send `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'; require-trusted-types-for 'script'` plus `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

findings.summary: No HSTS, no clickjacking protection (no frame-ancestors, no X-Frame-Options), and no Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. The page can be framed to overlay its personal-data form.
findings.evidence: headers primitive: strict-transport-security, x-frame-options, referrer-policy, permissions-policy all missing; no CSP, so no frame-ancestors.
findings.suggestedFix: Once on HTTPS send `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains`, CSP `frame-ancestors 'self'`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()`.

findings.summary: The one render-blocking stylesheet is served uncompressed and without cache headers, so every visit re-validates or refetches it.
findings.evidence: har-summary hygiene: base.css in missingCacheHeaders and uncompressedTextOver2KB (3179 B transferred, content-encoding none); it is the only renderBlockingCandidate (parser-inserted <link rel=stylesheet>, VeryHigh). Absolute impact is small (LCP 611ms on throttled mobile).
findings.suggestedFix: Serve CSS with gzip/brotli and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` on a fingerprinted filename (base.<hash>.css), or inline this small sheet in <head>.

findings.summary: Required fields are not marked, and errors rely only on the browser's transient validation bubble: there is no :user-invalid styling, persistent inline message, or aria-invalid.
findings.evidence: form-probe: labels read 'Attendee name', 'Email', 'Ticket' (no required indicator) although name and email are required; on submit, validationMessage is 'Please fill out this field.' (native bubble only); aria-invalid null on both; features census :user-invalid 0 and :user-valid 0; setting email to 'not-an-email' yields only the native message.
findings.suggestedFix: Per required-field-feedback: mark required fields in the label ('Attendee name (required)'), add an inline error element per field linked with aria-errormessage, show it with `input:user-invalid + .error-msg { display:block }` and a non-colour cue, and sync aria-invalid on blur/submit with a few lines of JS (progressive enhancement).

findings.summary: The attendee-name field has no autocomplete token, so autofill cannot offer the user's name. The email field is correct.
findings.evidence: form-probe: #name autocomplete null; #email autocomplete 'email' (type=email).
findings.suggestedFix: Add autocomplete="name" to #name (or autocomplete="off" with a hint if registrants usually enter someone else's name), and spellcheck="false" on the email field.

findings.summary: Ticket tiers (standard / accessible / student) are offered with no price, eligibility, or explanation, and there is no information on what registering commits the user to or how to cancel.
findings.evidence: form-probe: ticket options standard/accessible/student with value = label; no currency, 'price', 'free' or 'cost' text anywhere on the page; no cancellation or refund wording; no confirmation step exists (F01).
findings.suggestedFix: State each tier's price (or 'Free') and who qualifies in the option text or an adjacent description (aria-describedby), say what 'accessible' provides, and add how to cancel or transfer a place. Show the chosen tier and total on the confirmation page. With only three tiers, the forms guide recommends visible radio buttons over a <select> so all options and their prices are scannable at once.

findings.summary: The event date is ambiguous free text with no year and no machine-readable <time>. As of this audit (2026-10-09), 'Sunday 7 June' matches 2026, a date that has already passed.
findings.evidence: dom/form-probe: <dd>Sunday 7 June, 10am</dd>, 0 <time> elements; ar-EG/Asia/Tokyo render is text-identical (no locale-aware formatting). 7 June is a Sunday in 2026 (past at audit time); the next 'first Sunday in June' is 6 June 2027.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark up `<time datetime="2027-06-06T10:00">Sunday 6 June 2027, 10am</time>` (or the intended year), with the year always included. For an event venue, store the date with its IANA zone (per coordinate-global-events) and render the visible text in the venue's local time.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Heap 30049 -> 32063 nodes, 1.02MB -> 1.12MB self size. The growth is V8 code/closures/shapes from compiling the injected probe script, since the page itself has 0 scripts and no listeners to retain anything; no Detached* constructors in the post snapshot.

checkOutcomes.method: heap baseline totals + DOM element count
checkOutcomes.evidence: ~1.0MB JS heap self size (engine baseline only) and 44 DOM elements, proportionate to a static form page.

checkOutcomes.method: heap constructor comparison for Detached* + script/listener inventory
checkOutcomes.evidence: No Detached* constructors in baseline or post-interaction summaries; 0 scripts means no page event listeners, intervals or observers can accumulate.

principleOutcomes.reason: No agent-facing surface or declared agent intent on a small community event page; both checks judged not-applicable with rationale (opportunity noted: agentic-forms).
